name: Eicher Motors Ltd
title: Eicher Motors Ltd - 505200 - Audio Recording Of Conference Call

read.thesis: Royal Enfield output ramped to 4,500/day in June and 5,000+ now, Cheyyar brownfield to 1.5m with Tada 2.45m by FY30 reaffirmed; channel stock at 10-12 days, 4-5 days of savings targeted.

triggers.label: Tada greenfield INR1,225 cr approved
triggers.quote: the Board has approved an investment of INR1,225 for the Phase 1 of the greenfield at Tada

summary.headline: Eicher Motors Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32% YoY to INR 6,632 crore and PAT 21% to INR 1,463 crore, led by Royal Enfield volumes.
summary.overview: Royal Enfield sold 332,940 units in Q1 FY27 versus 261,326 a year earlier, with 301,174 in India and 31,766 exports. Consolidated revenue was INR 6,632 crore (vs INR 5,042 crore) and EBITDA INR 1,591 crore (vs INR 1,203 crore), with PAT of INR 1,463 crore including INR 168 crore of share of associate profits. VECV (commercial vehicles) sold 24,815 units, up 14.8%, with revenue of INR 6,610 crore and EBITDA of INR 541 crore (8.4% margin vs 9.2%). Management announced a INR 1,225 crore greenfield plant at Tada, Andhra Pradesh, and a Cheyyar brownfield expansion to a 2 million-unit capacity path.

financial_highlights.change: +21% YoY vs INR 1,205 crore; includes INR 168 crore share of associate profits
vs INR 511 crore YoY; margin 8.4% vs 9.2%
Partly due to Q4 ad spend and launch timing shifting out of Q1

segments.name: Royal Enfield (motorcycles)
segments.commentary: Sold 332,940 units (+27% YoY); 350cc volumes reportedly growing about 34%, while 450cc and 650cc are at an early stage of recovery after GST-related pricing changes. Flea (city+ mobility brand) launched C6 deliveries in Bengaluru with 100+ vehicles sold in about two months.

segments.name: VECV (commercial vehicles)
segments.commentary: Record 24,815 units (+14.8%) and 14.8% share in light, medium and heavy segments combined; buses 6,126 units with Volvo buses/trucks at a record 598 units. Revenue INR 6,610 crore and EBITDA margin 8.4%, down from 9.2%.

segments.name: Non-vehicle business (Royal Enfield)
segments.commentary: Accounts for about 15.3% of Royal Enfield revenue in Q1, up from 13.7% in Q4; service job cards up 20% YoY, averaging about 9 per month.

guidance_outlook: Management is optimistic of growth in the remaining quarters of FY27, with no numeric guidance given.
Management is tracking about 30% growth in domestic demand indicators (bookings, walk-ins, telephone inquiries) and declined to give forward margin guidance.
Tada, Andhra Pradesh greenfield: INR 1,225 crore Phase 1 approved, adding 4.5 lakh units per year at full utilisation, expected to complete in FY29-30 in modules.
Cheyyar (VECV) brownfield: INR 958 crore announced Feb 2026; total capacity to reach 2 million units by FY27-28, with the greenfield path taking capacity to 2.45 million by FY29-30.
Management expects the Royal Enfield daily delivery rate to reach 5,000-5,100 per day, with Cheyyar module-1 ramp by October.
capex_capacity: Board approved INR 1,225 crore for Phase 1 of the greenfield plant at Tada, Andhra Pradesh, adding about 4.5 lakh units per year at full utilisation.
Cheyyar brownfield (VECV): INR 958 crore announced Feb 2026; current capacity about 1.5 million units, targeting 2 million.
Royal Enfield produced 1.16 lakh vehicles in June; daily build reached 4,500 per day, with Oragadam and Vallam running three shifts since April.
Supplier base to run 24/7 three-shift operations to support the ramp to 5,000+ per day.
Setting up own CKD facility in Brazil; CKD plant under consideration for Indonesia.
demand_pricing: Royal Enfield 350cc volumes up about 34%; 350cc new variants and colourways (Tarmac Black, Mumbai Yellow, Moonshot White) drew strong response, with the premium Hunter variant at 50% of Hunter buyers.
450cc sells about 2,400-2,500 units per month and 650cc about 4,200 per month, per management; the segment is showing early recovery.
ASP rose on price actions: 1.75% on most 350cc models from April 2026 (benefit 1.2%) and 0.85% on certain models in January; mix benefit about 0.2%.
Input cost inflation (aluminium, crude, steel, copper, precious metals) and logistics disruption had a net impact of 4-4.5% of input costs; engineering/VAVE benefits about 0.4%.
Customer mix: about 70% upgraders, 25% first-time buyers, 5-6% existing owners buying an additional bike.

Exports: Brazil is the largest export market, with volumes up 3x in three years; every fourth exported motorcycle goes to Brazil. Europe is in an adjustment phase with distributor pressure; Riders Club numbers exceeded 42,000.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Cheyyar brownfield, labour issues and channel inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Production hit 4,500 per day in June with 1.16 lakh units; the ramp to 5,000+ per day delivery is underway. Dealer inventory is 10-12 days, and management aims to save 4-5 days by cutting secondary transit and billing dealers directly.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin pressure and the lower expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Input cost inflation of 4-4.5% was partly offset by a 1.75% price hike on 350cc models. Expenses were 7% lower, reflecting Q4 ad spend (INR 20 crore) and launch costs (INR 10 crore) that did not recur, plus INR 22 crore of controlled spending; management declined to give forward margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the early read on Flea and the demand outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Flea's Jayanagar store sold 100+ C6 vehicles in two months, with buyers averaging 25-30 years old; management is expanding to 10 Bengaluru touchpoints before other cities. Domestic volumes are tracking about 32% growth.

qa_highlights.question: How will the festive season and the likely GST-linked demand surge be handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management tracks about 30% growth in demand indicators and plans to build inventory via three-shift vendor operations, with Cheyyar module 1 ramp by October.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the consolidated PAT gap to standalone widen, and what drives subsidiary profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiaries (notably Brazil) are profitable; the gap is offset by export revenue booked in India. Subsidiaries are 8-9% of volumes, against a 0.8-1 million unit opportunity outside India.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Average gross block rose by about INR 346 crore, mainly from new capitalisation (including tools and dies) for the recent launches.

risks_watch: Inventory and dealer stock at 10-12 days; execution on the Cheyyar ramp to 5,000+ per day and the October module.
Input cost inflation (aluminium, crude, steel, copper) and the margin hit from pricing actions, with no forward guidance given.
Possible GST-related demand shifts for the industry from September/October, creating high-volatility conditions in the second half.
Indonesia CKD plan: quota restrictions and 160%+ luxury tax above 250cc.
VECV EBITDA margin fell to 8.4% from 9.2%; watch heavy-duty bus weakness.
Flea scaling: early and limited customer data.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and capacity expansion, with management calling the outlook optimistic for the remaining quarters. They were cautious on margins and forward guidance, citing volatile input costs and declining to give a forward outlook.

adds.what: Tada, Andhra Pradesh greenfield Royal Enfield plant Phase 1, 4.5 lakh units/yr at full utilisation
Cheyyar (VECV) brownfield expansion from ~1.5 million to 2 million units/yr

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management is optimistic on remaining FY27 quarters and tracks ~30% domestic demand indicators, backed by Royal Enfield daily rate rising to 5,000-5,100 (from 4,500), Cheyyar module-1 ramp by October and Tada INR 1,225 cr Phase 1 approved (live FY29-30).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Input cost inflation of 4-4.5% of input costs and a 1.75% price hike (benefit 1.2%) leave VECV EBITDA margin down to 8.4% from 9.2%, and management declined to give forward margin guidance.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Cheyyar brownfield (INR 958 crore, Feb 2026) is under construction, module-1 ramp due by October, and capacity moves from ~1.5m to 2m units by FY27-28; Royal Enfield daily build already at 4,500 with three shifts running at Oragadam and Vallam.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Royal Enfield Q1 volumes up 27% YoY to 332,940 units, domestic demand indicators tracking ~30% growth, and daily delivery rate targeted at 5,000-5,100 from 4,500.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Build rate of 4,500-5,000 per day runs near full capacity with three shifts already in place, and Tada Phase 1 (INR 1,225 crore) is approved but further steps such as Brazil CKD and an Indonesia CKD plant are under consideration.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is optimistic on the remaining FY27 quarters and tracks ~30% domestic demand growth, but gives no numeric guidance to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Possible GST-linked demand shifts from September/October create high volatility in H2, and input cost inflation (aluminium, crude, steel, copper) remains unpriced in guidance.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Flea is expanding to 10 Bengaluru touchpoints before other cities after 100+ C6 sales in two months, and 350cc colourways and variants drew strong response (350cc volumes up ~34%).

rows.label: Brazil CKD facility and Indonesia CKD plan
rows.why: Own CKD facility being set up in Brazil (largest export market, every fourth exported motorcycle) and an Indonesia CKD plant is under consideration, though Indonesia faces quota limits and 160%+ luxury tax above 250cc.

rows.label: Dealer inventory reduction via direct billing
rows.why: Dealer inventory is 10-12 days and management aims to save 4-5 days by cutting secondary transit and billing dealers directly.

rows.label: Supplier three-shift operations and VAVE savings
rows.why: Supplier base moving to 24/7 three-shift operations for the 5,000+ per day ramp, and engineering/VAVE benefits of about 0.4% are already flowing.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand (~30% domestic indicator growth), Cheyyar ramp and capacity expansion, but cautious on margins and declined forward margin guidance amid volatile input costs; analysts pushed on margins, the expense decline and subsidiary profitability.
